summary.one_liner: A C workshop that walks you through building a basic Unix shell, covering process launching, builtins, and pipes.
summary.what_it_does: This is a tutorial-style workshop README rather than a finished shell, with numbered exercises that guide the reader through writing one. It starts with a read-eval loop that prompts for a line and echoes it back, then uses execvp to run commands with arguments through a provided parse_command helper. It explains fork and wait so the shell returns to its prompt after each command. It adds a cd builtin implemented with chdir, explaining why a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. It ends with pipelines, using pipe, dup2, and a fork_and_exec_with_io helper to connect two commands. The final section lists extensions to try (longer pipelines, file redirection, environment variables, globbing, background jobs) without providing solutions.
use_cases: learn how unix shells launch processes
build a toy shell in C as a course exercise
understand fork, exec, and wait system calls
learn how pipes connect commands with dup2
understand why cd must be a shell builtin
stack: POSIX system calls (fork, execvp, wait, pipe, dup2, chdir)
notable: Explicitly scoped to process launching and pipes, leaving out parsing, memory management, and error handling
Step-by-step exercises with diagrams of process state across fork and exec
Ends with a list of natural extensions: redirection, longer pipelines, globbing, background jobs, job control
Explains the reasoning behind the cd builtin using process metadata
caveats: Skeleton code and utility functions are referenced as a TODO link and are not included in the README
Job control and some sections are marked TODO
Relies on POSIX system calls, so it is Unix-only
README does not name a license
